subject: Re: Brightline launch window - request for temporary p95 measurement carveout
messages:
From: Jamie Torres <jamie.torres@brightline.health>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@brightline.health>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Observed p95 spikes during launch window - can we get an exception?

Hi Hannah,

Quick note from our ops team after yesterday's staged launch: we're seeing consistent p95 latency spikes to ~1.3s for text-gen calls during a 20–30 minute burst when a new feature toggles go live. The p50 stays stable at ~120ms.

This traffic is predictable (we have a coordinated rollout at 09:00 PT) but the spike pushes us over the contracted p95 target in the hosted API addendum. We flagged this to our customer success team and wanted to ask if Redwood can offer a short-term measurement carveout for the scheduled launch windows while we iterate on client-side throttling and batching.

I've attached a short summary and a traffic graph. We'd propose either a temporary exception for the 09:00–09:30 launch window for two weeks, or a carveout that excludes the first N minutes of a planned deploy. Happy to jump on a call.

Thanks,
Jamie Torres
Director of Platform Reliability
Brightline Health

Attachments: brightline-launch-spike-summary.pdf, burst-traffic-graphs.png

Hi Jamie —

Appreciate the heads up and the crisp data. Short answers up front: yes, we can discuss a temporary carveout, and we'll need a clear traffic profile and exact launch schedule to scope it (start/end times, expected RPS, whether bursts are single-region).

What we'll do next:
- Karthik (cc) will propose a technical carveout definition (timebox vs. daypart exclusion vs. tagged deploy events).
- We'll draft an exception amendment you can share with your procurement/legal teams if we land on language.
- If this is recurring, we should evaluate an autoscale/dedicated capacity path as a more durable fix.

Can you send the per-minute RPS for the last three launches and confirm the timezone for the 09:00 window? If possible, attach the rollout runbook the ops team uses. I'll pencil a 30-min slot tomorrow to walk through.

Subject: Re: Observed p95 spikes during launch window - can we get an exception?

Jamie / Hannah —

Dug into the preliminary traces Marissa uploaded to INF-7891. A few quick technical notes to help shape the exception language:

- The observed behavior (stable p50, transient p95 spikes) is classical high-burst tail latency when many short requests hit the model in a tight window. Because p95 is a tail metric, very short-lived bursts can dominate the slice if not windowed appropriately.

- Two reasonable approaches:
  1) Timebox carveout: exclude a deterministic 30-minute launch window from p95 computation for up to two weeks while client-side mitigations roll out.
  2) Traffic-tag carveout: mark requests during flagged deploys with a header (X-Deploy-Event) and exclude tagged requests from SLA measurement.

- Measurement details to propose for the amendment: p50 target: 150ms (native), p95 target: 600ms (hosted API), measurement bucket: 5-minute rolling windows aggregated over 24 hours; carveout applies only to scheduled launch windows provided with >=24h notice.

- Caveat: we cannot retroactively exclude unnotified bursts. Also, if burst traffic becomes the normal traffic pattern, carveouts will be rejected and we'll recommend switching to Dedicated pools for guaranteed capacity.

I'm happy to draft the technical section for the amendment. If you approve, I'll add the quantification and link to INF-7891 for evidence.

—Karthik

Subject: Proposed temporary exception amendment — review & signature request (BR-9941)

Jamie / Samir —

Per our conversation and Karthik's technical proposal, please find attached a draft amendment that:

- Defines temporary exclusion windows for scheduled launches (default 30 minutes per launch) for up to two consecutive weeks.
- Requires >=24 hours notice from Brightline Ops with per-minute RPS attached to qualify for exclusion.
- Specifies measurement buckets (5-min rolling windows aggregated daily), and reiterates p50/p95 baselines for the hosted API.

Next steps we need from Brightline:
1) Confirm whether you prefer the timebox approach or the X-Deploy-Event header approach.
2) If timebox, please populate the attached "launch schedule" tab and return the document; if header, confirm that your deploy tooling will set X-Deploy-Event for scheduled releases.
3) Approve and counter-sign the amendment via DocuSign: https://redwood.app/docusign/BR-9941-exception

If you want, we can make the exception retroactive to the last three launches while you work the client-side batching; note our legal team will only accept retroactivity if Brightline provides the per-minute evidence for those launches.

I'll leave Karthik and Marissa on thread to finalize the technical appendix once you pick an approach.

Thanks —
Hannah
